risks: refusedReanchor now labels every error of the re-anchor loop that is not ErrTargetNotFound as ErrInvalidMarkdown, so 400. Most of those errors are the caller's markdown, because the scratch document holds only the uploaded tree. Three of MarkWriter.Mark's guards are not: an unknown mark.Type (markTypes), attrNestingError over the stored mark's attributes, and an empty range (pmdoc/find.go:1042-1050). Each of those reads the stored anchor rather than the upload, so if one ever fired the caller would be told its markdown is at fault. I could not reach any of them: a mark type outside markTypes cannot be in a mark the finder found, since MarkWriter wrote every mark in the room and checks the same set. Recording it rather than calling it a defect; the reviewer may want it on the Not proven / risk line.

The 200-upload room test's retained figure is noisy at this scale: 134,856 B, 135,232 B and 387,568 B across my three runs of the same code (674 B, 676 B and 1,938 B per upload). The bound holds with at least 5.8x margin in every run, and the main-side control is two orders of magnitude away (489,536 B per upload), so the verdict does not turn on the noise - but a single number from one run should not be read as precise.
